Laura —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The execs liked the latency/cost profile and we're close on commercial terms, but Legal has a couple of open items in the Order Form related to IP and training use we need to resolve before procurement can sign. High level questions from our counsel: 

- Section 5 (Output ownership): can you confirm Redwood's stance on customer-generated output — OmniCorp wants explicit assignment of output for productization within their internal apps (not public resale).
- Section 9 (Feedback & training license): Legal is asking whether data submitted via API (including prompts/feedback) can be used to further train models, and if so, under what protections (anonymization, opt-out).
- Exhibit A (Telemetry/telemetry retention): they want a short carveout guaranteeing telemetry with PII stripped will not be used to train models for 24 months.

I've attached the redline they gave us (Omni_Requested_Redlines.docx). Could you and your legal partner confirm what language we can accept vs where we need counters? Procurement is aiming to get this to signature next week.

Sophie

Sophie —

Appreciate the clear summary and the redline. Quick responses up front to help your team triage: 

- Output ownership: Redwood's default approach is to grant a broad, perpetual right to customers to use output produced by the service for their internal business purposes, including productization in their own internal apps and services. We cannot assign our underlying model weights or derivative rights to third parties, but we can add contract language that says OmniCorp will own customer-generated outputs for internal use and redistribution to its end customers (please see proposed wording below).

- Feedback/training license: We do not ingest customer data for training by default for hosted customers. For Hosted/Managed deployments we require an explicit opt-in for training. We can offer an affirmative opt-out clause and an operational separation for telemetry used for platform improvement vs model training, with a 24-month holdback for telemetry containing potential PII.

- Telemetry retention carveout: We can accept a 24-month restriction for telemetry-derived training signals that are not fully anonymized; any telemetry used for low-level runtime improvements (e.g., kernel selection, perf metrics) will be retained but not used for model training.

I've pasted suggested contract language below (short form) and attached a PDF with redline markers to the Omni draft. If those points look acceptable I can loop Legal (Ben) to produce final MSA/Order Form edits. If Omni needs assignment of outputs beyond internal productization (e.g., sublicensing to third parties), that's a material change and we'll need to scope it with our Legal and Product teams.

Proposed short clauses (for your review):

1) Output Rights: "Customer owns the output it inputs into and receives from the Services for Customer's internal business use and distribution to Customer's end users. Redwood retains ownership of the underlying models, model weights, and training data. Customer shall not receive ownership of Redwood's models or any derivative rights to redistribute models as models."

2) Training & Feedback License: "Redwood will not use Customer content to train or improve Redwood models for other customers unless Customer provides explicit, written opt-in. Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for platform health and performance improvements, subject to the telemetry retention/holdback clause below."

3) Telemetry holdback: "Telemetry that may contain PII or user-generated identifiers will not be used for model training for a minimum of 24 months from collection. After 24 months, telemetry may only be used for training if it has been processed to remove or irreversibly anonymize personal identifiers."

Next steps: Ben, Monica — can you review and propose precise redline language for the Order Form's Sections 5 & 9 and Exhibit A? Sophie, happy to set a quick call today if Omni Legal wants to walk through specific redline assets.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Ben / Monica —

Forwarding Omni's reply and Marcus' asks. High-level proposed positions so we can craft redline: 

1) Channel/reseller sharing: Agree to allow Omni to distribute outputs to its channel partners provided that: (a) outputs are derived solely from Omni-owned input data; (b) Omni's partners are bound by equivalent restrictions not to claim ownership of Redwood models; and (c) Redwood receives notice if outputs will be redistributed publicly (to protect model IP). Proposed clause to add: "Customer may share Customer Output with its resellers and channel partners solely for the purpose of Customer's provision of services to its end users, provided such resellers agree in writing to terms no less protective of Redwood's IP than this Agreement."

2) "Irreversibly anonymize" definition & audit right: We can accept a narrow audit right limited to scope and frequency (e.g., one reasonable audit per 12 months, with redactions and NDA), and define irreversibly anonymize as removal of direct identifiers and application of irreversible hashing/aggregation so data cannot be reconstructed to a single user. We should push back on broad, continuous audit rights.

3) Call: Yes, 10am PT tomorrow works for Legal. Sophie, Marcus — please send calendar invite. Ben / Monica please prepare a redline with exact edits for Sections 5 & 9 and Exhibit A; I'll review before the call.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
